\subsection{Mechanisms Read Off the Data}
\label{sec:exp_mechanism}

\textbf{Question.} Not a further RQ but a display: two mechanisms that \S\ref{sec:exp_prediction} argues from fitted scores, and one collection property behind \S\ref{sec:exp_analysis}, shown on the recorded readings.
\textbf{Setup.} Figure~\ref{fig:two_futures} and Figure~\ref{fig:mechanism}(a,b) describe collected readings, not model skill, so no value in them is comparable with a skill score; Figure~\ref{fig:mechanism}(c) reads the paired contrasts of Table~\ref{tab:prediction}.  % CALIBER; reading rules returned to the captions 2026-09-21

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.92\linewidth]{figs/fig_two_futures.pdf}
\caption{One reading is consistent with two opposite next steps. For each task, the next change against the current reading, split by the direction of the step before it; faint marks are transitions and each line is the mean of its group in eight equal-width bins. Transitions whose previous step was flat carry no direction and are dropped, which removes 7\% of transitions on sentiment and up to 66\% on Joint-2.}  % figs/_fig_report.json fig_two_futures n_flat_dropped over n_up+n_down
\label{fig:two_futures}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Findings, why a window helps.} At a fixed reading the next change differs with the direction of the previous step on all four tasks (Figure~\ref{fig:two_futures}).  % m1; figs/_fig_report.json fig_two_futures separations: Joint-3 +0.100, Joint-2 +0.070, sentiment +0.058, sentence length +0.025 (shown in the figure)
The separation does not rank the tasks the way the memory gain does: sentence length carries the largest gain in Table~\ref{tab:prediction} and the smallest separation here.  % n_main_013 (+0.603) vs +0.025
Read with \S\ref{sec:exp_memory}, that ordering points at the per-item level rather than the turn-to-turn trend as the larger part of what the window buys.  % m6

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.92\linewidth]{figs/fig_mechanism.pdf}
\caption{What the command channel carries, and what a learned lifting costs. (a) and (b) Applied command against tracking error, on the two Table~\ref{tab:prediction} tasks that log a per-turn command; colour marks the target and repeats the vertical position, which is the point. (c) Paired $\mathrm{Skill}_H$ contrast of the linear case over the learned lifting, on all seven tasks, grouped by readout dimension: a circle marks the five one-dimensional readouts, a square the two-dimensional one and a diamond the three-dimensional one. A filled marker means the 95\% interval excludes zero; the dagger marks a caveated entry.}
\label{fig:mechanism}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Findings, what the command channel carries.} In Figure~\ref{fig:mechanism}(a,b) the applied command holds the value of the target across the full range of the tracking error, on every recorded transition of both tasks.  % m5; 2268/2268 sentence length, 240/240 sentiment; error span [-0.40, +0.88]; counts moved to App. A7 on 2026-09-21
This is the collection property behind the command-channel scope of \S\ref{sec:exp_analysis} and Appendix~\ref{app:A7_command_channel}.  % nc_1; nc_8

\textbf{Findings, what a lifting has to find.} The cost of a learned lifting concentrates on the one-dimensional readouts and is close to zero on the two multi-dimensional ones (Figure~\ref{fig:mechanism}c).  % c2; n_main_183 n_main_111 n_main_135 (one-dimensional: +0.599, +0.101, +0.048); n_main_031 n_main_047 (multi-dimensional: +0.014, +0.005)
The cost does not fall with the number of trajectories: the largest sits on the task fit on 100 trajectories and the smallest on the task fit on 90.  % n_main_183 (n=100) vs n_main_047 (n=90)
The driver is that a one-dimensional readout leaves a lifting little structure to expose, which is the part of the mechanism these seven columns support.  % m4; this is the single statement of the lifting driver (removed from 4.2 on 2026-09-21)

Together, \uline{the window separates two opposite next steps at one reading, and the cost of a lifting tracks the dimension of the readout rather than the amount of data.}
